paper.title_en: Mathematics of effective q-plate in polarization optics
paper.abstract_en: The q-plate is a spatially inhomogeneous SU(2) birefringent optical element that has garnered significant interest due to its ability to mediate the spin-orbit interaction of light and facilitate the generation of structured light with singularities. The q-plate features a spatially varying fast axis orientation defined by three parameters: the topological charge q, retardance delta, and the offset angle $alpha_0$. While the parameter alpha_0 can be changed many times by rotation, any change in the charge and/or retardance entails the fabrication of a new plate. This limitation can be overcome through the concept of an effective waveplate, where multiple waveplates, homogeneous or inhomogeneous, are aligned coaxially so that, under specific constraints, the composite system emulates the behavior of a single effective waveplate. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical formalism for realizing an effective waveplate through a cascaded configuration of three q-plates, each chosen as either a quarter-wave q-plate, a half-wave q-plate, or a combination thereof. Some configurations offer tunability of the retardance over the full range from 0 to $2pi$, even though q-plates with fixed retardances of $pi/2$ and pi are used in sequence to form an effective q-plate. This feature enables holonomic polarization walk on the higher-order Poincare sphere. Such a capability holds significant potential for applications involving structured light associated with the higher-order Poincare sphere, particularly in controlled polarization transformations and polarization-topology engineering.
